summary: Robin Coningham is an archaeologist and Indologist. Supervised by Frank Raymond Allchin, he completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge and King's College in 1994. He held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (from 2005).

Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University around 1980 and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University starting around 1993.
Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College, Oxford, and earned his doctorate under John Hurrell Crook around 1974. He held an academic post at University College London from around 1987 to 1994.
Roderick Henry Macleod was an Indologist. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge around 1914–1915, where he also served as Lecturer in Indian Law in 1913.

Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown and Harvard universities (PhD ca. 1942). He taught at the Barnes Foundation (1946) and Brown University (ca. 1947–1987), served as Honorarprofessor at Graz (1974), and edited Philosophy and Phenomenological Research.

Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He served on the faculty at the University of Queensland from around 1976 to 2002, where he was an Associate Professor from around 1990 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he is an emeritus professor (attested 2011).

Roger Billard was an Indologist who studied under Louis Renou at INALCO and the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He worked in the manuscript department of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1945–1951) and at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1952–1979).

Roger Bischoff is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin, and served as an Assistant Teacher at the International Meditation Centre (attested 1995).

Roger Brown was a linguist who completed his studies at the University of Michigan between 1946 and 1952. He subsequently held a long-term academic appointment at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Goossens was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Université libre de Bruxelles around 1926, studying under Émile Boisacq, Paul-Émile Dumont, and Henri Grégoire, and became Professor of Greek there in 1945.

Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris and the Science Faculty of Paris. He was affiliated with the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle from around 1929 to 1970, serving as its director between roughly 1951 and 1965.
Roger Jeffery is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Edinburgh by 1985. He has held a post there since 1972, eventually becoming Professor (Emeritus).

Roger R. Jackson specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at Wesleyan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1983) under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, he held faculty posts at Fairfield University (attested 1986) and Carleton College (attested 1990–2017).

Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and Sinologist. He earned his PhD from SOAS under D. C. Lau in 1978 and had a long career at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1978–2016), also editing Philosophy East and West.

Rohana Seneviratne is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who earned degrees from Peradeniya, Liverpool, and Oxford (DPhil 2015). Seneviratne served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Peradeniya from 2022 to 2024.
Rohit Saluja works in the fields of computational studies and Indology, and has held positions at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Roland Barthes was a French philosopher and linguist who studied under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1959), the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).

Roland Ferenczi is an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Pécs and Eötvös Loránd University. In 2024, he held posts at the Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences and as an MSCA Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Hamburg.

Roland Grubb Kent was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania in 1903, where he taught comparative philology from 1902 to 1947, and lectured at Bryn Mawr (1910–1914).
